rule: The C++ sets no hit-stop, shake, flash, sound or knockback. Hit reactions are authored in the Havok behaviour graph as named events (HitFrame, CamHit, blockHitStop, staggerStart, FlinchStart, recoilLargeStart) and magnitude variables (staggerMagnitude, recoilMagnitude); the engine that orders them is not in the box. The one timing rule in the code is a fallback window: value = min + mult * (max - min), with mult from the combat style, distance floored at twice the bound radius, and wait taken from graph variables with the game's setting as fallback.
keep: one scalar per style rescaling a min and max window
distance floor at twice the body radius
change: no hit feedback to keep; hit-feedback decision is nothing to adapt
our names, our numbers, server fixed tick instead of graph timing
look_test: Two enemies in the Pit with the same body and style scalar 0.2 and 0.9. Watch attack then back-off. The low scalar should hold ground and wait briefly; the high scalar should step far back and wait longer. Judge at 375 wide whether the difference reads without a label.
